title: The Clockmaker's Puzzle
summary: A young apprentice in old Damascus must figure out why a grand clock keeps jamming before an important deadline, solving the puzzle through careful observation.
poll: Careful observation is more useful than quick guessing when solving a hard problem.

versions.title: The Clockmaker's Puzzle
versions.text:
Yusuf is an apprentice. He works with Hassan in a small workshop. Hassan makes clocks. Yusuf wants to learn too.

Hassan is making a big clock. A leader wants the clock. He needs it soon. It must be done in three days. There is not much time.

But the clock has a problem. Its gears stop. They stop at the same spot. No one knows why. Hassan feels upset.

Hassan tries to fix it. He makes the gears tight. He adds oil. Still, it stops.

Yusuf has an idea. He watches the clock turn. He watches it again and again. He is careful. He listens close.

At last, Yusuf finds it. One gear has a bent tooth. It is made of wood. It hits the next gear.

Yusuf shows Hassan. They fix the tooth. Now the clock works! They send it to the leader. Hassan is glad.

versions.title: The Clockmaker's Puzzle
versions.text:
Yusuf is an apprentice who works with Hassan in a small workshop in a busy old city. He hopes to learn the craft too, just like Hassan.

Hassan has been making a big clock for the city leader. The leader wants it done in three days, so there is not much time to spare.

But the clock has a strange problem. The gears stop at the same spot every time, no matter how it is wound. No one can tell why this keeps happening, and it upsets Hassan a great deal.

Hassan tries a few fixes. He makes the gears tight and checks each part by hand. Still, the clock stops at the same spot every time.

Yusuf has an idea. He watches the clock turn, again and again, as careful as he can be. He leans in close and listens for small sounds inside it.

Finally, after many tries, Yusuf finds something small that no one else had seen. One wooden gear has a bent tooth, and that tooth hits the gear beside it every time it turns.

Yusuf shows Hassan exactly what he found. Together, they file the bent tooth down until it is smooth and even again.

Now the clock turns round and round without ever stopping! Hassan lets out a long breath of relief and smiles at Yusuf.

They send the clock to the leader just in time, and it keeps good time from that day on. Hassan tells Yusuf that sharp, still eyes can solve even the hardest puzzle a workshop will ever face.

versions.title: The Clockmaker's Puzzle
versions.text:
Yusuf was an apprentice who worked with Hassan, a clockmaker, in a workshop in old Damascus. The city was known for its skilled makers. Hassan followed a tradition begun by Al-Jazari, who had built water clocks long ago.

Hassan had taken on an important commission: a clock for the city leader, due in only three days. There was no time for mistakes.

Soon, the clock's mechanism began to fail. Every time it was wound, the gears would jam at the same spot. No one could explain why, no matter how Hassan adjusted it.

Hassan tried many fixes. He tightened each gear. He checked each part by hand. Still, the clock jammed in the same spot every time.

Yusuf decided to observe the clock instead of rushing to fix it. He watched it turn again and again, listening for quiet, precise sounds inside the gears.

After many tries, Yusuf noticed something tiny. One wooden gear had a tooth that was bent, and it kept hitting the metal gear beside it.

Yusuf showed Hassan what he found. Together, they filed the bent tooth until it was smooth and even. When they wound the clock again, it did not jam at all.

They gave the clock to the leader just in time. Hassan told Yusuf that patient watching, not hurried guessing, was how Al-Jazari himself had built his famous water clocks long ago.

versions.title: The Clockmaker's Puzzle
versions.text:
Yusuf was an apprentice who worked with Hassan, a clockmaker, in a workshop in old Damascus, a city known for its skilled makers and engineers. Hassan followed a tradition begun by Al-Jazari, who had built amazing water clocks many years earlier using gears, floats, and flowing water.

Hassan had taken on an important commission: a fine clock for the city leader, due in only three days. There was no time at all for careless mistakes, since the leader was known for his impatience.

Soon, the clock's mechanism began to fail in a frustrating way. Every time it was wound, the gears would jam at the very same spot. No one, not even Hassan, could explain why this kept happening.

Hassan tried everything he could think of to fix it. He tightened each gear, checked every part by hand, and oiled the whole clock, hoping it would finally run smoothly. Still, the clock jammed in the same spot every single time it was tested.

Rather than rushing to fix it the way his master had, Yusuf decided to observe the clock patiently. He watched it turn again and again, leaning close to listen for the quietest, most precise sounds hidden inside the gears.

After many tries, Yusuf finally noticed something tiny that no one else, not even his master, had seen. One wooden gear had a tooth that was slightly bent, and it kept hitting the metal gear beside it.

Yusuf showed Hassan exactly what he had found, pointing at the bent tooth under the lamp. Together, they filed it down, bit by bit, until it was smooth and even once more.

When they wound the clock again, it turned round and round without jamming once. Hassan let out a long breath of relief and smiled proudly at his young apprentice.

They gave the finished clock to the leader right on time, and it kept good time after that. Hassan told Yusuf that patient watching, not hurried guessing, was how Al-Jazari himself had built his famous water clocks long ago, studying each small part before changing anything.

versions.title: The Clockmaker's Puzzle
versions.text:
Yusuf was an apprentice clockmaker who worked for Master Hassan in a modest workshop in Damascus, a city long known for its skilled craftsmen and engineers. Master Hassan followed a tradition that began with Al-Jazari, a twelfth-century engineer who had built remarkable water clocks using gears, floats, and carefully channeled water.

Master Hassan had taken on an important commission: a large, ornate clock for the governor's palace, due in only three days. There was no time at all for careless mistakes, since the governor was known throughout the city for his impatience.

Soon, the clock's mechanism began to fail in a deeply frustrating way. Every time it was wound, the gears would jam at the very same point, no matter how carefully Master Hassan adjusted them beforehand.

Master Hassan tried everything he could think of to fix the problem. He tightened each gear, loosened others experimentally, and added fresh oil, hoping the mechanism would finally run smoothly. Still, the clock jammed in the same spot every single time it was tested.

Rather than rushing to guess at a fix the way his master had, Yusuf decided to observe the clock patiently, sure that the answer was hiding in plain sight. He watched it turn again and again, leaning close to listen for the quietest, most precise sounds hidden inside the gears.

After many careful tries, Yusuf finally noticed something tiny that no one else, not even his master, had seen. One wooden gear had a tooth that was slightly bent, and it kept catching on the metal gear positioned directly beside it.

Yusuf showed Master Hassan exactly what he had found, pointing at the bent tooth under the lamplight. Together, they filed it down, bit by bit, until it became smooth and even once more.

When they wound the clock again, it turned round and round without jamming once. Master Hassan let out a long breath of relief and smiled proudly at his young apprentice, clearly impressed.

They delivered the finished clock to the governor's palace right on time, and it kept perfect time from that day forward. Master Hassan told Yusuf that patient observation, not hurried guessing, was exactly how Al-Jazari himself had designed his famous water clocks long ago, studying each small part carefully before changing anything.

versions.text:
In the city of Damascus, long renowned for its skilled craftsmen and inventive engineers, an apprentice named Yusuf worked for a clockmaker named Master Hassan in a modest workshop tucked among the narrow streets. Master Hassan had learned his craft from a lineage of clockmakers who followed the tradition established by Al-Jazari, a brilliant twelfth-century engineer whose innovations in water-powered clocks had been celebrated throughout the Islamic world and studied admiringly by scholars and craftsmen for centuries afterward.

When Master Hassan accepted an important commission for an intricate clock destined for the governor's palace, he was given only three days to complete it, a deadline that left no room whatsoever for careless mistakes, especially given the governor's well-known impatience with any sort of delay. Almost immediately, however, the clock's mechanism began failing in a deeply frustrating manner: every time it was wound, its gears would jam at precisely the same point, no matter how meticulously Master Hassan adjusted them beforehand, as though some invisible obstacle were quietly resisting his every effort.

Master Hassan tried everything he could think of, tightening each gear individually, loosening others experimentally, and adding fresh oil in the hope that the mechanism would finally run smoothly, yet the clock jammed at the same spot every single time it was tested, regardless of what he changed. Rather than rushing to guess at a fix the way his master had, Yusuf chose instead to observe the clock patiently, convinced that the true answer was hiding somewhere in plain sight among its many intricate parts, and he watched it turn again and again, leaning close to listen for the quietest, most precise sounds hidden deep within the gears.

After many painstaking attempts, Yusuf finally noticed something tiny that everyone else, including his own master, had overlooked entirely: one wooden gear had a tooth that was slightly bent, and that single tooth kept catching against the metal gear positioned directly beside it, interrupting the mechanism's rhythm at the exact same instant every time it turned. When Yusuf showed Master Hassan exactly what he had discovered, pointing carefully at the bent tooth under the lamplight, the two of them worked together to file it down meticulously, bit by bit, until it became smooth and precisely even once again, matching the shape of its neighboring teeth perfectly.

When they wound the clock a final time, it turned round and round without jamming even once, and Master Hassan let out a long breath of relief before smiling proudly at his young apprentice, clearly impressed by his patience and his growing ingenuity as an engineer in training. They delivered the finished clock to the governor's palace exactly on time, and its mechanism kept perfect time from that day forward, a quiet triumph built entirely on careful looking rather than hurried guessing.

Master Hassan told Yusuf afterward that this patient observation was exactly how Al-Jazari himself had built his own lasting legacy centuries earlier, carrying forward an innovation that generations of later engineers would continue to study, admire, and build upon long after his own lifetime had ended, proof that the smallest details, noticed carefully enough, could solve even the largest problems.

keyWords.definition: a machine that tells you what time it is
keyWords.example: We checked the clock before we left for school.

keyWords.definition: a wheel with teeth that turns another wheel inside a machine
keyWords.example: The toy car had a tiny gear inside it.

keyWords.definition: a room or building where someone makes or fixes things
keyWords.example: My uncle fixes bicycles in his workshop.

keyWords.definition: a young person learning a skill by helping someone who already knows it
keyWords.example: The apprentice baker learned to shape bread from the head baker.

keyWords.definition: paying close attention so you do not make a mistake

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?
options: An apprentice who fixes a clock's gears
A boy who learns to bake fresh bread every day
A leader who builds a brand-new palace downtown
A long trip to a busy market in the city
questions.why: The story follows Yusuf as he carefully watches a clock and finds the bent gear tooth that is causing it to jam.

wrong.B: The story is not about baking bread.
wrong.C: The leader asks for the clock but does not build a palace in the story.
wrong.D: There is no trip to a market in the story.

questions.stem: Who is Yusuf?
options: A leader who rules the whole city
An apprentice who helps Hassan
A farmer who grows wheat in his fields
A traveler who just arrived in the city
questions.why: The story says Yusuf is an apprentice who works with Hassan, a clockmaker.

wrong.A: The leader is a different character who wants the clock.
wrong.C: The story does not say Yusuf is a farmer.
wrong.D: The story does not say Yusuf is a traveler.

questions.stem: What does Hassan need to finish in three days?
options: A new house for his family
A long trip to the market in town
A big clock for the city leader
A simple wooden chair for the house
questions.why: The story says a leader wants the clock and needs it done in three days.

wrong.A: The story is not about building a house.
wrong.B: No trip to the market is mentioned.
wrong.D: Hassan is making a clock, not a chair.

questions.stem: Why does the clock stop every time it turns?
options: Someone keeps turning it off on purpose
It runs out of oil right away each day
The leader does not want it fixed yet
One gear has a bent tooth that catches
questions.why: Yusuf discovers that a bent wooden tooth on one gear keeps catching on the gear beside it.

wrong.A: No one turns the clock off on purpose.
wrong.B: Hassan adds oil, but that is not the real cause.
wrong.C: The leader wants the clock fixed, not left broken.

questions.stem: Why does Hassan feel upset about the clock?
options: He cannot find out why it stops
He does not want to make clocks anymore
Yusuf refuses to help him fix it
The leader canceled the whole job
questions.why: Hassan tries several fixes but cannot discover the real cause, which upsets him.

wrong.B: Hassan is clearly still working hard as a clockmaker.
wrong.C: Yusuf helps Hassan the whole time.
wrong.D: The job is not canceled; they finish it.

questions.stem: In the story, a gear is —
options: a round kind of clock face
a wheel with teeth in a machine
a cloth bag for carrying small tools
a tall tower made of soft sand
questions.why: The story describes a gear with a tooth that catches on the gear beside it, which is a wheel with teeth.

wrong.A: A clock face is different from a gear.
wrong.C: The story never calls a gear a bag.
wrong.D: There is no tower of sand in this story.

questions.stem: Why does Yusuf watch the clock again and again instead of guessing?
options: He is bored and has nothing else to do
Hassan told him to stop helping
He wants to find exactly what is wrong
The clock is too loud to ignore
questions.why: Yusuf watches closely and listens for small sounds because he wants to find the real cause of the problem.

wrong.A: Yusuf is trying hard to help, not avoiding work.
wrong.B: Hassan wants Yusuf's help the whole time.
wrong.D: The story does not say the clock is too loud.

questions.stem: What happens right after Yusuf finds the bent tooth?
options: The clock suddenly breaks completely
Hassan becomes even more upset
They immediately send the clock to the leader
Yusuf and Hassan fix the tooth together
questions.why: After Yusuf finds the bent tooth, he shows Hassan and they fix it together before sending the clock away.

wrong.A: The clock does not break; it is fixed.
wrong.B: Hassan is relieved, not more upset, once the cause is found.
wrong.C: They fix the clock first, and only then send it to the leader.

LOW.prompt: Do you think Yusuf was a good helper to Hassan? Explain why or why not, using at least two facts from the story.
checklist: I clearly said what I think.
I used at least two facts from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: I think Yusuf was a good helper. He watched the clock very carefully again and again until he found the bent tooth. He also worked together with Hassan to fix it instead of giving up. Because of Yusuf, the clock worked and they finished the job for the leader on time.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the story?
options: Patient observation helped Yusuf fix the clock in time.
Yusuf disliked working in the busy Damascus workshop.
Hassan decided to retire and give the shop to Yusuf.
Al-Jazari traveled to Damascus to teach Hassan directly.
questions.why: The story shows Yusuf solving the clock's jam by observing it patiently, in time for Hassan's deadline.

wrong.B: Yusuf works hard and seems to enjoy learning the craft.
wrong.C: Hassan does not retire in the story.
wrong.D: Al-Jazari lived long before the story and never visits Damascus in it.

questions.stem: What had Hassan accepted when the story begins?
options: A trip to visit Al-Jazari in his home
An important commission for a clock
A brand-new apprentice from another city
A request to teach at a nearby school
questions.why: The story says Hassan had taken on an important commission: a clock for the city leader.

wrong.A: Hassan does not travel to visit Al-Jazari in the story.
wrong.C: Yusuf is already his apprentice; no new apprentice arrives.
wrong.D: There is no school in the story.

questions.stem: How long did Hassan have to finish the clock?
options: Exactly one week
A whole month
Three days
Just one single day
questions.why: The story says the clock was due in only three days.

wrong.A: A week is longer than the time given in the story.
wrong.B: A month is far longer than the deadline in the story.
wrong.D: One day is shorter than the deadline given.

questions.stem: What kept happening every time the clock was wound?
options: It suddenly rang too loudly
The clock hands moved backward slowly
It ran perfectly every single time
Its gears jammed at the same spot
questions.why: The story repeats that the gears would jam at the same spot every time the clock was wound.

wrong.A: The story never mentions the clock ringing.
wrong.B: The hands moving backward is not described.
wrong.C: If it ran perfectly, there would be no problem to solve.

questions.stem: In the story, the word observe means —
options: to watch something closely
to fix something quickly
to sell something for money
to forget about a problem
questions.why: Yusuf observes the clock by watching it turn again and again and listening closely to it.

wrong.B: Yusuf avoids a quick fix and watches instead.
wrong.C: No selling happens in the story.
wrong.D: Yusuf does the opposite of forgetting about the problem.

questions.stem: Why did Yusuf decide to watch the clock instead of guessing at a fix?
options: Hassan firmly ordered him to stay completely quiet
He wanted to discover the real cause first
He truly did not care whether the clock worked
He wanted to avoid upsetting the impatient leader
questions.why: Yusuf chooses patient observation because he believes close watching will reveal the real problem.

wrong.A: Hassan never orders Yusuf to stay quiet.
wrong.C: Yusuf clearly cares, since he works hard to solve the problem.
wrong.D: The story does not describe Yusuf worrying about the leader's feelings.

questions.stem: What can you tell about Al-Jazari from the story?
options: He never built anything that actually lasted long
His methods still mattered to clockmakers later
He worked directly for the same city leader as Hassan
He was actually Yusuf's own older brother
questions.why: Hassan still follows Al-Jazari's tradition, showing that his methods mattered long after his own time.

wrong.A: Al-Jazari's water clocks are remembered as lasting achievements.
wrong.C: Al-Jazari lived long before Hassan's time, not alongside him.
wrong.D: The story never says Al-Jazari and Yusuf are related.

questions.stem: How does the story mostly unfold?
options: By carefully comparing two very different cities
By listing exact steps for oiling an old clock
By describing many different city festivals
By presenting a problem and then solving it patiently
questions.why: The story first presents the jamming clock as a problem, then shows how Yusuf's patient observation solves it.

wrong.A: The story stays in one city, Damascus.
wrong.B: The story is not a how-to list.
wrong.C: No festivals appear in the story.

MID.prompt: Explain how Yusuf solved the problem with the clock. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how Yusuf solved the problem.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Yusuf solved the problem by watching the clock patiently instead of guessing at a quick fix. He observed it turn again and again and listened closely for small sounds. This careful method helped him notice that one wooden gear had a bent tooth, which was jamming the mechanism. Once he and Hassan filed the tooth smooth, the clock worked perfectly, and they finished Hassan's commission on time.

keyWords.definition: having many small parts put together in a complicated way
keyWords.example: The spider wove an intricate web between two branches.

keyWords.definition: a person who designs or builds machines, structures, or systems
keyWords.example: An engineer designed the new bridge across the river.
The jeweler was meticulous when setting the tiny gemstones.

keyWords.definition: a new idea, method, or invention
keyWords.example: The new water pump was a major innovation for the village.

keyWords.definition: something important that a person leaves behind after they are gone
keyWords.example: The teacher's legacy lived on through her students' kindness.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the story?
options: Meticulous observation helped an apprentice solve an intricate problem.
Yusuf found engineering far too difficult and quickly gave up entirely.
Hassan built the whole intricate clock entirely by himself alone.
The governor firmly rejected the finished clock as completely unacceptable.
questions.why: The story centers on Yusuf's meticulous observation solving the intricate jam in time to meet the governor's deadline.

wrong.B: Yusuf never gives up; he persists until he solves the problem.
wrong.C: Yusuf helps Hassan solve the problem and fix it together.
wrong.D: The governor's palace receives the finished clock, and it keeps perfect time.

questions.stem: What tradition had Master Hassan learned his craft from?
options: A tradition of papermaking from Baghdad
A tradition established by Al-Jazari the engineer
A tradition of fine weaving passed down in Damascus
A tradition brought long ago by sailors from the coast
questions.why: The story explains that Master Hassan learned his craft from a tradition established by Al-Jazari.

wrong.A: Papermaking is not mentioned in the story.
wrong.C: Weaving is not part of this story.
wrong.D: No sailors appear in the story.

questions.stem: What was actually causing the clock's mechanism to jam?
options: A missing piece of oil in the mechanism
A broken spring hidden in the base
One gear tooth that was slightly bent
Sand that had blown inside the workshop
questions.why: Yusuf discovers that a single wooden gear tooth, slightly bent, kept catching on the gear beside it.

wrong.A: Oil was added, but it was not the real cause.
wrong.B: No broken spring is mentioned in the story.
wrong.D: Sand is not part of this story.

questions.stem: In the story, the word meticulous most nearly means —
options: careless, rushed, and hurried in approach
loud, confident, and sure of everything
confused, uncertain, and unsure what to do
extremely careful about small details
questions.why: The story describes Yusuf and Hassan filing the bent tooth meticulously, meaning with extreme care over small details.

wrong.A: Meticulous is the opposite of careless and hurried.
wrong.B: The word does not describe volume or confidence.
wrong.C: Meticulous work requires clear focus, not confusion.

questions.stem: Why does the story describe Yusuf as 'an engineer in training' near the end?
options: His careful approach showed real engineering skill
He had already completely and fully finished his training
He firmly planned to stop making clocks forever
He had secretly invented a brand-new kind of clock
questions.why: Yusuf's patience and careful attention to the mechanism's intricate parts mirror the qualities of a true engineer, even though he is still learning.

wrong.B: He is still an apprentice, so his training is not finished.
wrong.C: Nothing suggests Yusuf wants to stop making clocks.
wrong.D: Yusuf fixes an existing clock rather than inventing a new kind.

questions.stem: Why did Master Hassan's earlier fixes, like tightening gears and adding oil, fail to solve the problem?
options: The governor cancelled the commission before they finished
None of those fixes addressed the actual bent tooth
The clock was simply too old to ever be repaired at all
Al-Jazari's original design did not allow any repairs
questions.why: Tightening gears and adding oil never touched the real cause, the single bent tooth, so the jam kept returning.

wrong.A: The commission is not cancelled; it is completed on time.
wrong.C: The clock is successfully repaired, so it was not beyond repair.
wrong.D: The story never says Al-Jazari's designs cannot be repaired.

questions.stem: What does the story suggest about Al-Jazari's legacy?
options: It was forgotten soon after his death
It only ever mattered to people living in his own city
It continued to influence engineers for generations
It was eventually replaced by a completely different tradition
questions.why: Master Hassan still follows Al-Jazari's methods centuries later, showing his legacy continued to influence engineers.

wrong.A: His legacy clearly was not forgotten, since Hassan still follows it.
wrong.B: The story never limits his influence to one city.
wrong.D: Hassan continues the same tradition rather than replacing it.

questions.stem: Why does the story end with Master Hassan's comment about Al-Jazari?
options: To describe exactly how clocks are built, step by step, in detail
To criticize Yusuf for being too slow
To explain in detail the full history of the governor's palace
To connect Yusuf's method with an engineering tradition
questions.why: Ending with Al-Jazari links Yusuf's patient observation to a long, respected tradition of careful engineering.

wrong.A: The story does not give step-by-step building instructions.
wrong.B: Hassan praises Yusuf rather than criticizing him.
wrong.C: The palace's history is not the focus of this closing comment.

HIGH.prompt: Do you agree that patient observation is more valuable than quick guessing when solving a difficult problem? Support your argument with evidence from the story.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that patient observation is more valuable than quick guessing. In the story, Master Hassan's hurried fixes, like tightening gears and adding oil, never solved the real problem because he never looked closely enough to find it. Yusuf, by contrast, observed the clock meticulously and noticed the one bent tooth that was causing the jam. Someone might argue that quick action matters more when a deadline is near, but the story shows that rushing without understanding the true cause can waste time, while careful observation, in the tradition of engineers like Al-Jazari, actually solves the problem faster in the end.
